1	Instruction packet bootstrap: part 2/6
2	
3	- **Security / reliability:** XSS, injection (SQL/NoSQL/command), SSRF, path traversal; AuthZ/AuthN gaps, missing tenancy checks; secret leakage or API keys in logs/env/files; rate limits, unbounded loops, CPU/memory hotspots; unsafe deserialization, weak crypto, insecure defaults; race conditions, check-then-act, TOCTOU, missing locks. Call out both **exploitability** and **impact**.
4	- **Code quality:** error handling (swallowed exceptions, overly broad catch, missing handling, async errors); performance (N+1 queries, CPU-intensive ops in hot paths, missing cache, unbounded memory); boundary conditions (null/undefined, empty collections, numeric boundaries, off-by-one). Flag issues that may cause silent failures or production incidents.
5	- **Removal candidates:** propose deletion only when a demonstrated current cost or defect justifies it and required behavior is preserved. A pending task's unreachable scaffold or disabled feature is not, by itself, a removal candidate. Distinguish **safe delete now** vs **defer with plan** when removal is warranted. For warranted removals, provide concrete steps and proportionate validation checkpoints.
6	
7	### 7) Self-check and confidence assessment
8	
9	For **each finding** from Steps 5–6:
10	
11	1. Re-read the relevant code and surrounding context independently.
12	2. Ask: **"Could I be misreading the code?"** — trace execution paths, check for runtime behavior, configuration, or framework conventions that might make this correct.
13	3. Ask: **"Is this a real issue or a style preference?"** — distinguish between bugs/risks and subjective choices that don't affect correctness or security.
14	4. Ask: **"What's the actual impact?"** — verify that the severity matches the real-world consequence, not just the theoretical violation.
15	5. Assign final confidence score (1–100%) with **explicit reasoning** documenting:
16	   - What was verified
17	   - What evidence supports the finding
18	   - What uncertainty remains
19	6. Downgrade or **remove** findings that don't survive the self-check.
20	
21	### 8) Index findings
22	
23	Index any P0/P1 findings that suggest a systemic or structural pattern (not isolated typos or one-off mistakes) as `kk:review-findings`. Index on first encounter — recurrence detection happens on the search side in future reviews.
24	
25	- If no P0/P1 systemic findings exist, explicitly note "No findings to index" and move on.
26	- This step is mandatory — do not skip it even if the review found no issues.
27	
28	### 9) Present results
29	
30	#### Output format
31	
32	Structure your review as follows:
33	
34	```markdown
35	## Code Review Summary
36	
37	**Files reviewed**: X files, Y lines changed
38	**Overall assessment**: [APPROVE / REQUEST_CHANGES / COMMENT]
39	**Intent and scope**: requirement source, current task/request, selected diff and candidate state
40	**Baselines**: review base/candidate; separate release baseline if applicable
41	
42	## Behavior and Compatibility
43	
44	Inspected paths/scenarios, observed results and evidence limits. Include applicable
45	Supported / Blocked / Unknown / Not applicable conclusions with named baselines.
46	Attribute author-supplied results and inherited issues. Record outstanding evidence
47	or release prerequisites, next actions and durable tracking locations when deferred.
48	
49	---
50	
51	## Findings
52	
53	### P0 - Critical
54	
55	(none or list)
56	
57	### P1 - High
58	
59	- **[file:line]** Brief title
60	  - Profile: {profile_name} · Checklist: {checklist_filename}
61	  - Triggered by: {signal_type} — {signal_description}
62	  - Trigger/path, expected vs actual result and consequence
63	  - Confidence: 90% - reasoning behind the confidence level
64	  - Suggested fix
65	
66	- **[another_file:line]** Brief title
67	  - Profile: generic · Checklist: —
68	  - Triggered by: —
69	  - Trigger/path, expected vs actual result and consequence
70	  - Confidence: 60% - reasoning behind the confidence level
71	  - Suggested fix
72	
73	### P2 - Medium
74	
75	...
76	
77	### P3 - Low
78	
79	...
80	
81	---
82	
83	## Removal/Iteration Plan
84	
85	(if applicable)
86	
87	Only include recommendations tied to a demonstrated issue or an identified,
88	currently required verification gap. A clean scoped review needs no extra work.
89	```
90	
91	**Inline comments**: Use this format for file-specific findings:
92	
93	```
94	::code-comment{file="path/to/file" line="42" severity="P1"}
95	Description of the issue and suggested fix.
96	::
97	```
98	
99	Apply [functional-review.md](functional-review.md)'s verdict mapping: a hard acceptance/delivery violation cannot be approved; material Unknown evidence receives COMMENT absent a demonstrated blocker. Out-of-scope operational unknowns do not automatically downgrade an explicitly scoped code verdict. Preserve P0–P3 impact severity and distinguish code correctness from release readiness.
100	
101	**Every review** reports coverage and limits, even with findings. When no issues are found, explicitly state:
102	
103	- What was checked
104	- Any areas not covered (e.g., "Did not verify database migrations")
105	- Specific residual risks or required verification gaps, when supported
106	
107	### 10) Close the review or handle required next steps
108	
109	Close with the scoped verdict and coverage. When no substantiated issue or
110	required evidence/prerequisite needs action, state that no changes are recommended
111	for the reviewed increment. Omit remediation menus and invitations to start
112	pending work.
113	
114	For a substantiated inherited defect surfaced in the report, give one concrete
115	separate follow-up when its repair is outside the reviewed task; do not make that
116	repair a condition of approving an otherwise supported increment. In-scope
117	findings and required evidence/prerequisites retain their corrections or next
118	checks. Ask which actions to take only when the current request
119	has not already authorized them; an invoking implementation request may already
120	cover fixes. Review-only work still does not authorize edits.
121	
122	Apply the same evidence threshold to every suggestion, including optional notes
123	and proposed menu choices. A rejected hypothetical concern does not become valid
124	by moving it out of Findings or offering it as future preparation. Retain material
125	unknowns and the common method's conditional verdicts; this closing branch does
126	not waive unverified requirements.
127	
128	### 11) Verify outputs
129	
130	Before declaring the review complete, check each item in the **Required Outputs** section of SKILL.md:
131	
132	- [ ] Review report presented to user
133	- [ ] Intent, scope/baselines, inspected behavior, applicable compatibility conclusions and evidence limits reported
134	- [ ] P0/P1 systemic findings indexed as `kk:review-findings` (or explicitly noted "No findings to index")
135	- [ ] Required next steps handled, or clean review closed without proposing new work
136	
137	If any item is unchecked, go back and complete it before proceeding.
138	
139	END SOURCE

145	# Capy Knowledge Base Protocol
146	
147	If `capy` MCP tools are not available in this session, skip all search and index steps below and proceed normally.
148	
149	## Source Label Taxonomy
150	
151	All plugin-managed labels use the `kk:` namespace prefix.
152	
153	| Label                    | Contents                                                              |
154	| ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
155	| `kk:arch-decisions`      | Architecture decisions, design rationale, trade-offs                  |
156	| `kk:review-findings`     | Code review patterns, recurring issues, anti-patterns                 |
157	| `kk:lang-idioms`         | Language best practices, idiomatic patterns from external sources     |
158	| `kk:project-conventions` | Discovered project patterns, naming conventions, structural decisions |
159	| `kk:test-patterns`       | Testing approaches, edge cases, test infrastructure decisions         |
160	| `kk:debug-context`       | Root causes, tricky bugs and their fixes, environment gotchas         |
161	
162	## Search Conventions
163	
164	- Use 2-4 specific terms per query — not vague keywords
165	- Always scope with `source` filter to relevant `kk:*` labels
166	- Use `source: "kk:"` only for broad cross-domain searches (e.g., CoVe verification)
167	- Default `limit: 3` per query unless more context is needed
168	- **Cold-start fallback:** If no results, proceed with standard guidelines — empty results are normal for new projects
169	
170	## Index Conventions
171	
172	- Only index non-obvious learnings not derivable from reading the code or git history
173	- Keep content concise — summarize the insight, don't dump raw output
174	- Always use a `kk:` prefixed label from the taxonomy above
175	- One concept per `capy_index` call — don't bundle unrelated learnings
176	- Skip indexing if the insight is already captured in design docs or CLAUDE.md
177	
178	END SOURCE

184	## Profile detection procedure
185	
186	Single source of truth for computing the set of profiles active in the current context.
187	Consumed by six skills: `/kk:review-code`, `/kk:review-spec`, `/kk:design`, `/kk:implement`, `/kk:test`, and `/kk:document`.
188	
189	Every profile under `klaude-plugin/profiles/<name>/` declares its own trigger rule in `DETECTION.md` using the mandatory three-section schema (`## Path signals`, `## Filename signals`, `## Content signals`).
190	The shared procedure below applies the same algorithm against every profile's declared values.
191	
192	### Inputs per consuming skill
193	
194	Not every consumer has a diff available. Use the input listed for your skill:
195	
196	- **`/kk:review-code`** — git diff (staged, or an explicit commit range). Scope is
197	  the set of files the diff touches.
198	- **`/kk:review-spec`** — git diff when invoked standalone; the feature directory's
199	  full file list when invoked by `/kk:implement` (spec review runs over the whole
200	  feature, not just the current task's diff).
201	- **`/kk:test`** — git diff mid-feature, OR the feature directory's file list
202	  post-implementation.
203	- **`/kk:implement`** — the current sub-task's target file list, augmented by the
204	  diff accumulated so far in the feature.
205	- **`/kk:design`** — **no file list available** (implementation does not yet exist).
206	  Detection uses a user-declared or keyword-inferred signal instead; see
207	  [The `/kk:design` interaction pattern](#the-design-interaction-pattern) below.
208	- **`/kk:document`** — feature directory's current file list; diff optional.
209	
210	### The `/kk:design` interaction pattern
211	
212	The design phase runs before any code exists, so file-based detection is impossible. Detection uses idea-prose keyword matching against tokens declared in each profile's `DETECTION.md`.
213	
214	**Algorithm:**
215	
216	1. **Collect tokens.** Iterate §Known profiles. For each `<name>`, `Read` `${TOOLBOX_PLUGIN_ROOT}/profiles/<name>/DETECTION.md`. If the file has no `## Design signals` section, skip — that profile does not participate in design-phase detection. Otherwise, parse `display_name` and `tokens` from the section.
217	2. **Build union.** Collect all declared tokens into a single set, each tagged by its source profile name and `display_name`.
218	3. **Match.** Check the idea prose against the union. Matching is case-insensitive, whole-word (so `pod` in "podcast" does not fire).
219	4. **Confirm.** On match, surface a confirmation prompt per matched profile:
220	   *"This appears to be a {display_name} feature. Activate the {profile_name} profile?"* — let the user confirm yes/no. When multiple profiles match, confirm each independently.
221	
222	END PACKET PART 2/6
